submission.natural_language_explanation: N1146+ fires on the initial letter of an as-yet-unidentified capitalised word: it peaks on a lone capital-letter token that opens a name, place, heading or list entry (' G' in Glyn / Gijs / Göttingen / G20, ' T' in Triceratops / Tee, 'P' in Pius or in Practice after a paragraph break), and is far weaker when the same letter sits inside a word or acronym ('IgG1', 'PLG'), when the word continues inside the token (' Gear', ' Paris', ' The'), on lower-case letters, or when the lone capital is used as a symbol ('Vitamin C', 'grade A'). The trigger is lexical rather than positional (mid-sentence onsets after 'by', 'with', 'and' or '4.' fire as strongly as line starts), and letter identity matters a lot: lone G, P, T, L, B, R, A, I, E and J fire, while C, D, K, Q, S, V, X and Z are actively suppressed.

rival_explanations: It is a plain token-identity detector for a fixed set of single-letter tokens: it fires wherever those exact token ids appear and the word-onset, line-start and proper-noun effects I claim are merely where such tokens concentrate.

It is a structure detector for formatted text: it fires on the first token of a new line or entry (wiki markup, tables, list items, headings), and the lone capital letters are just the commonest first tokens of such lines, so a lowercase line start in the same markup should fire too.

It is an uncertainty neuron that fires where the next-token distribution is most open after an unfamiliar word onset, independent of which letter was read (next-token entropy at these onsets correlates r = +0.48 with the pole), so letters with high entropy after them should fire and low-entropy ones should not.

readings.explanation: N1146+ fires on the initial letter of an as-yet-unidentified capitalised word: it peaks on a lone capital-letter token that opens a name, place, heading or list entry (' G' in Glyn / Gijs / Göttingen / G20, ' T' in Triceratops / Tee, 'P' in Pius or in Practice after a paragraph break), and is far weaker when the same letter sits inside a word or acronym ('IgG1', 'PLG'), when the word continues inside the token (' Gear', ' Paris', ' The'), on lower-case letters, or when the lone capital is used as a symbol ('Vitamin C', 'grade A'). The trigger is lexical rather than positional (mid-sentence onsets after 'by', 'with', 'and' or '4.' fire as strongly as line starts), and letter identity matters a lot: lone G, P, T, L, B, R, A, I, E and J fire, while C, D, K, Q, S, V, X and Z are actively suppressed.

It is a plain token-identity detector for a fixed set of single-letter tokens: it fires wherever those exact token ids appear and the word-onset, line-start and proper-noun effects I claim are merely where such tokens concentrate.

It is a structure detector for formatted text: it fires on the first token of a new line or entry (wiki markup, tables, list items, headings), and the lone capital letters are just the commonest first tokens of such lines, so a lowercase line start in the same markup should fire too.

It is an uncertainty neuron that fires where the next-token distribution is most open after an unfamiliar word onset, independent of which letter was read (next-token entropy at these onsets correlates r = +0.48 with the pole), so letters with high entropy after them should fire and low-entropy ones should not.
